falcon-theatre: The box office and Will Call open one hour before performances. Online sales close one hour before curtain; the box-office phone takes voicemail at 513-479-6783.
Box Office/Will Call opens 1 hour prior to each performance.
Box Office telephone line is available at all times via voice mail (513) 479-6783.
Online ticket sales close 1 hour prior to curtain for all performances.

Falcon lists public parking at 707 Monmouth Street beside The Pepper Pod, 7th and Orchard behind La Mexicana Grocery, and 117 E. 5th Street behind Truist Bank. Its directions page does not establish step-free connections or designated accessible spaces in those lots.
Public Parking Lots 117 E. 5th Street, behind Truist Bank 707 Monmouth Street, next to The Pepper Pod 7th Street and Orchard, behind La Mexicana Grocery

Falcon’s health page asks patrons who feel ill to contact the box office about transferring or refunding tickets if necessary. It welcomes masks and says a hand-sanitizer station is available in the lobby.

If you are feeling sick or demonstrating ANY signs of illness, please stay home. Contact the Falcon Theatre Box Office with regards to tickets you may have purchased and we will either transfer or refund your tickets if necessary. MASKS WELCOME : All Patrons entering Falcon Theatre are welcome to wear masks if it makes you feel more comfortable to do so. A hand sanitizer station will always be available in the lobby.
fitton-center-for-creative-arts: Fitton lists a mobility-device-accessible pottery wheel and ramp access to its movement studio. The page does not give wheel clearances, ramp dimensions or the route from the elevator.

Fitton’s camp procedures ask anyone needing accommodations for an education program to contact the Director of Education & Outreach before registering. This is an advance discussion, not confirmation that a particular accommodation is arranged.
If a student believes that they will require accommodations to enable them to participate in our programs, please contact our Director of Education & Outreach before registration.
cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden: The zoo lists adult changing tables in two sensory-friendly family restrooms at Vine Street Village and two at the Picnic Shelters. It gives a height of 31 inches and a 400-pound capacity for these tables; a transfer board is available at the Welcome Center. These are published specifications, not Threshold measurements.
Vine Street Village 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs; transfer board available in Welcome Center)
Picnic Shelters 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs)

Each calming room accommodates one family at a time, first come, first served. The rooms stay locked until an employee opens them. Ask an employee, visit the Welcome Center or call 513-475-6198; if a room is occupied, staff can suggest alternative calm spaces.

Each Calming Room can accommodate one family at a time, on a first-come, first-serve basis. To utilize the Calming Room at any point during your Zoo visit, please contact any employee, visit the Welcome Center, or call our Visitor Experience team at 513-475-6198. They will give you directions to meet an employee in the entry area. The door to the Calming Rooms is locked and can only be accessed by an employee. If the Calming Room is in use when you request it, the Visitor Experience team will advise alternative locations for a calm space.

The courtesy cart returns from the Grove food-truck area to Vine Street Village. Request it through Public Safety at 513-475-6112 or the Guest Services podium across from Mai Thai’s Marketplace. It is not a continuously running shuttle and may involve a wait.

This cart has a predetermined path starting from the Grove food truck area back to Vine Street Village. To request the Courtesy Cart, please contact Public Safety at (513)475-6112, or visit the Guest Services Podium across from Mai Thai’s Marketplace. This service is not a constantly running shuttle, and you may experience a brief wait time.
The courtesy cart takes one mobility device at a time; some devices may not fit under the manufacturer’s safety rules. It cannot be reserved for groups, and service is first come, first served.

The Courtesy Cart can accommodate 1 mobility device at a time. Please note that due to manufacturer safety regulations, some mobility devices may not fit on the cart. The Courtesy Cart is not available for group reservation.
The Zoo offers a Courtesy Cart service for those with mobility concerns who need assistance returning to the front of the Zoo and is on a first-come first-served basis.
If you need a rental wheelchair to enter the zoo, ask a parking attendant for help retrieving one. The zoo warns that wheelchair availability varies and is not guaranteed.

If you plan to rent a manual or electric wheelchair and need it to enter the Zoo, please alert a parking attendant and they will assist you with retrieving one (availability of wheelchairs may vary and is not guaranteed).

The zoo gives the ordinary Safari Train boarding step as 19 inches and the doorway as 14 inches wide by 51 inches high. Its separate wheelchair car holds one wheelchair, with a ramp boarding doorway listed as 32 inches wide by 50 inches high; ask an employee for boarding and wheel-lock assistance.
Boarding the train requires visitors to step up 19” and to clear a 14”w x 51”h entry into the car.

The Safari Train has an accessible train car that can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. The accessible car is 56″ long and 37″ wide. Boarding the train using our accessible ramp requires visitors to clear a 32”w x 50”h entry into the car. To use the accessible train car, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.

The carousel can take one wheelchair at a time with staff ramp-boarding and wheel-lock assistance. For both train and carousel, some personal mobility devices may require transfer to a zoo-provided manual wheelchair because of the rides’ specifications.

The Conservation Carousel can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. To ride the carousel in a wheelchair, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.

Note: due to the manufacturer and safety specifications of our train and carousel, some personal mobility devices may not be allowed on the accessible section of our rides and may require guests to transfer to a Zoo provided manual wheelchair.

The zoo cannot refrigerate food or medicine; visitors may bring a cooler for items that need to stay chilled. Case-by-case storage of medical items is a separate service: ask at the Welcome Center or email at least two days ahead to coordinate.

The Zoo is unable to provide refrigeration of any kind for any items that may need to be kept cool. We advise that if you require certain items (food or medicine) to be kept chilled, you may bring in a cooler with you.

The Visitor Experience team may be able to store medical equipment or a cooler for medical needs on a case-by-case basis. For more information about storing medical items or places to comfortably administer these items, please visit the Welcome Center upon arrival, or email [email protected] at least (2) days prior to your visit to coordinate.
Cups of water are free at open dining locations. The zoo says its drinking fountains are turned off for the winter season; an open fountain should not be assumed during a winter visit.
Cups of water are available at no cost at any open dining location. Water fountains are available throughout the Zoo (these are turned off during the Winter season).

Ask for an Access Pass at the Welcome Center, train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience or Roo Valley. Staff give a lanyard with a return time based on the queue; return at or after that time and hand it to staff for the separate entrance.

To use an Access Pass, ask an employee at the Welcome Center, train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience, or Roo Valley for a pass: they will calculate the wait time and give you a lanyard with the time you are allowed to ride/enter the experience. At or after your time has passed, bring the lanyard to an employee at the ride or experience, and they will take it and allow you onto the next ride or experience through a separate entrance.
kings-island: The attraction-access program does not waive ride requirements: the park says every guest must meet each attraction’s height and health restrictions. Guest Services asks questions about the physical criteria needed for the requested rides.
All Guests are required to meet all riding requirements for every attraction, including height and health restrictions, to safely ride/participate.
Some questions are asked to ensure that the Guest has the required physical criteria in order to safely experience attractions.
After requesting ASL interpretation in advance, check in at Guest Services on arrival to review the show schedule and choose performances.
Upon arrival at the park, please check in with Guest Services to review our show schedule and determine your preferred showtimes and selections.

During WinterFest, temperatures near freezing may stop some rides from operating under manufacturer guidelines. Cold weather can also affect live entertainment; admission does not establish that a particular experience will run.

Please be advised that as temperatures approach freezing some rides may not be able to operate due to manufacturer guidelines. Colder temperatures also could impact live entertainment during WinterFest.
